newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch impose quarantine on livestock from E.Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dutch impose quarantine on livestock from E.Europe.

text.p: The Dutch agriculture ministry said on Monday it had imposed temporary quarantine restrictions on imports of livestock from eastern Europe due to fears over the spread of foot-and-mouth disease.
A ministry spokesman told Reuters farm animals from throughout eastern Europe would be subject to tests for the disease following its discovery last week in six shipments.
He could not give a precise list of countries affected.
"The animals will be held in quarantine while we test blood samples," he said.
The measure covers all livestock. In addition, pigs will be tested for signs of classical swine fever due to a severe outbreak of the disease in the Netherlands.

Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen was also approaching the European Commission to discuss possible EU-wide action, the spokesman added. Most of eastern Europe's livestock imports enter the EU through Germany.

Imports of livestock from eastern Europe into the Netherlands have surged in the past few months due to the swine fever epidemic, which has so far affected almost 300 farms and led to the destruction of some three million pigs.
